text:
Owen Power is finally playing like the first overall pick Buffalo hoped for. He's logging 25:18 a night, up from 21:39 last season, and he's on the ice for 32% of the Sabres' power-play chances, up from 12%. The result: 17 points in 22 games, 0.77 a game against 0.36 last season.

Some of that is a hot start. Our talent range for him still sits below his current scoring pace. But the luck around him has actually run the other way: Buffalo has scored 6.7 fewer goals than its chances deserve with him on the ice, and that usually swings back.

He's a passer first. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him at 6.9 primary shot assists per 60 last season, 96th percentile among defensemen. When he does shoot it can matter: in Chicago on Nov 12 he opened the scoring with a one-timer off a Josh Norris setup, as The Athletic's Matthew Fairburn described it, in a game Buffalo lost in overtime.

What to watch: his minutes have dipped to about 23.5 over the last ten games and his points with them. Whether the big role sticks is the real breakout question.
headline: Owen Power has the job he was drafted for
